results.title: China black mass import regulation to take effect on Aug 1 | Mysteel
results.content:
According to the announcement, qualified recycled black mass raw materials for lithium-ion batteries will not be classified as solid waste and can be imported freely. Specially, the recycled black mass must not be mixed with other types of recycled raw materials during shipment.    No bulk shipments are permitted, and different categories of recycled black mass must be separately packaged. The same customs declaration form cannot include multiple types of recycled raw materials. [...] The HS code for recycled black mass raw materials for lithium-ion batteries is 3824999996.

The announcement will take effect starting August 1, 2025.

Appendix: Performance Requirements for Recycled Black Mass Raw Materials for Lithium-Ion Batteries

results.content: But why this workaround? Black mass, a critical material for India’s energy transition, is a hazardous waste, legally classified under HSN heading 8549 - electrical and electronic waste and scrap. (Waste and scrap of primary cells, primary batteries ) By this classification Customs & DGFT restrict its trade, requiring recyclers to obtain a license from DGFT, which is issued only after approval from MOEF due to its hazardous nature. results.title: New Black Mass Export Rules: Will They Help or Harm the Lithium-ion Industry
results.content:
> For purposes of this Directive Allocation Order, ‘black mass’ means any shredded lithium-ion battery scrap that contains cathode material (which may include lithium, cobalt, nickel and manganese), anode material (graphite, silicon) or other residual battery cell materials.

While that definition explains what black mass is made of, it doesn’t show why it’s critical to the domestic supply chain or where and how it fits into the lithium-ion industry. [...] A recycler’s feedstock comes from two main sources: end-of-life batteries, or manufacturing scrap generated during production. Manufacturing scrap is further split into two categories: dry scrap (foil clippings and components produced before electrolyte is added) and wet scrap (material rejected after the electrolyte is injected).
